elements.text: Operator's failure to adequately inspect the former military turbine-powered helicopter
Engine issue progressing to loss of engine power
Loss of control after striking powerlines during forced landing
FAA's inadequate inspection and maintenance standards for former military turbine-powered aircraft with experimental exhibition airworthiness certificates
Operator's use of inadequate FAA standards instead of more rigorous standards readily available
FAA's inadequate oversight of the operator, failing to detect inherent risks
Helicopter structures and systems and weather conditions were not factors
Engine lost power necessitating emergency autorotation, pilot unable to maintain control after striking powerlines
Loss of engine power resulted from No. 2 bearing failure due to degraded radial support from exhaust diffuser cracks and rear bearing cover separation
FAA erred by allowing former military turbine-powered rotorcraft to be inspected/maintained under Part 43 Appendix D via 2011 Memorandum of Deviation
FAA allowed helicopter to continue being maintained/inspected under inadequate standards despite revisions, due to non-expiring exhibition certificates
Operator likely aware of more stringent inspection procedures for UH-1-series helicopters and should have used them
Engine exhaust diffuser cracks and rear bearing cover separation could have been detected with more frequent inspection intervals
Operator's failure to inspect engine using more frequent intervals and rigorous standards
Recurrent inspection involving removal of exhaust diffuser cover would increase probability of detecting damage for Ozark Aeroworks T53-series engines
Operator's failure to replace tail rotor blades exceeding life limits demonstrated inadequacy of maintenance procedures
Program letters are a necessary tool for FAA surveillance and operator compliance
Lack of guidance in FAA Order 8900.1 for routine surveillance was a factor in FSDO's failure to perform surveillance
Implementation of Safety Recommendation A-21-9 would result in bolstered regulations and safety enhancements
